question: What are the large systems in which quantum effects have been successfully demonstrated?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer frames the demonstrations as examples of macroscopic quantum mechanics probing the quantum–classical boundary, organized into two main platforms: (a) matter-wave interference of massive particles/molecules and (b) quantum control of macroscopic mechanical resonators.
examples: Quantum effects such as superposition have been pushed to ever larger systems to explore the boundary between quantum and classical realms
Two platforms: interfering large molecules and a quantum drum resonator

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that de Broglie matter-wave superposition was first established for small particles such as electrons, atoms, dimers, small van der Waals clusters, and neutrons, as the historical baseline.
examples: Superposition of matter waves has been observed for electrons, atoms, dimers, small van der Waals clusters, and neutrons
Before large-molecule experiments, neutrons and atomic clusters were among the most massive interfering particles

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies the C60 fullerene interference experiment (1999, diffraction at a material absorption grating) as demonstrating wave behavior in the most massive and complex object at that time.
examples: In 1999, interference of C60 molecules was observed by diffraction at a material absorption grating
C60 became the most massive and complex object with observed wave behavior

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer cites matter-wave interference of functionalized oligoporphyrins with masses beyond 25,000 Da and up to 2,000 atoms, observed in a new 2-m-long Talbot–Lau interferometer, as the heaviest objects to exhibit matter-wave interference.
examples: Oligoporphyrins of mass >25 kDa with up to 2,000 atoms showed interference fringes in a 2-m Talbot–Lau interferometer
The interferometer accommodates particles with a large variety of internal states across a wide mass range

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies a macroscopic mechanical resonator (microwave-frequency 'quantum drum' oscillator) cooled to its quantum ground state using conventional cryogenic refrigeration and coupled to a qubit for quantum-limited readout.
examples: A mechanical mode was cooled to its quantum ground state using a microwave-frequency mechanical oscillator coupled to a quantum bit
The 'quantum drum' resonator was cooled by conventional cryogenic refrigeration and measured via the coupled qubit

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that single quantum excitations (phonons) were controllably created in the mechanical resonator, demonstrating first steps toward complete quantum control of a macroscopic mechanical system.
examples: Researchers controllably created single phonons in the resonator
Single-phonon excitations demonstrated quantum-level manipulation of a macroscopic mechanical system

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer supports the interference claims with quantitative details: fringes reached over 90% of expected visibility in excellent agreement with quantum theory, and de Broglie wavelengths as short as 53 fm, five orders of magnitude below the molecules' diameter.
examples: Interference fringes reached more than 90% of the expected visibility, in excellent agreement with quantum theory and not explainable classically
The molecules' de Broglie wavelengths were as short as 53 fm, five orders of magnitude below their diameter

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that C60's many excited internal degrees of freedom and environmental couplings make it nearly a classical body, so interference experiments with such molecules enable detailed studies of decoherence.
examples: C60 is almost a classical body due to its internal degrees of freedom, making interference experiments useful for studying decoherence
Couplings to the environment essential for decoherence can be probed with large-molecule interferometry

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that increasing the mass and macroscopicity of superpositions places more stringent bounds on modifications of quantum mechanics such as objective collapse models.
examples: The 25 kDa superposition, with macroscopicity value 14.1, places an order-of-magnitude improvement in bounds on objective collapse models
Heavier interfering particles constrain modified quantum theories

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer situates matter-wave interferometry within the broader development of atom interferometric techniques for fundamental physics, precision metrology, and lithography.
examples: Atom interferometric techniques have been developed for fundamental quantum mechanics, metrology, and lithography
Matter-wave interferometry also underpins precision metrology applications
